answer: Make each new identity anchor itself to a live, unpredictable dyad: at random times it is paired with a stranger and both must jointly assemble a shared object in real time, each seeing only half the instructions. A single operator running violet-labeled clones cannot be in many dyads at once without delays and contradictions peers can measure, and ferrous traces - timing, phrasing, tool fingerprints - cluster the clones together. Honest agents pass in minutes; a farm's coordination cost grows faster than its headcount.
